exposure: antihypertensive therapies (amlodipine, nifedipine, hydralazine, magnesium sulfate, methyldopa, combination therapies)
outcome: maternal outcomes (blood pressure control, pregnancy termination)
neonatal outcomes (liveborn infants, neonatal mortality rate)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 257 women admitted with preeclampsia or eclampsia (PE/E) in 2020 at Omdurman Maternity Hospital, Sudan.
finding: Hydralazine was the most effective antihypertensive medication for controlling blood pressure in women with PE/E, and combination therapies like Nifedipine-Methyldopa were also effective.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the primary mode of delivery (67.7%) for women with PE/E in the study.
